title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Auth, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: This reference consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls for RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, Secure SDLC controls, incident response for security events, evidence collection workflows for audits, and the process for managing risk exceptions. Intended for engineering, security, product, and compliance stakeholders.
purpose: Provide a single, actionable source of truth describing required controls, owners, timelines, and runnable procedures to meet internal security policy and external compliance commitments (SOC2, ISO27001, customer contractual controls).
scope: Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane components, customer data stores, production inference runtime, CI/CD pipelines, and supporting infrastructure. Customer-specific private deployments should map these controls to their environment and submit deviation requests where required.
ownership_and_contacts: Primary owner: Security Engineering (security@redwood.example.com). Secondary owners: Eng-Infra, Eng-SRE, Product. Emergency contact: on-call security pager and SEV channel. Compliance evidence requests: compliance@redwood.example.com.
rbac_overview: We enforce a least-privilege RBAC model across cloud accounts, internal services, and the Redwood Console. Roles are defined for organizational and service scope and granted via groups in the corporate IdP (Okta). Service principal and machine identities follow separate lifecycles with stricter controls. Key roles: Owner, Org-Admin, Infra-Engineer, Platform-Operator, Service-Owner, Developer, Auditor, Read-Only-Support, Service-Account.
rbac_details_and_lifecycle:
- Role assignment: All human role assignments originate from groups in the IdP (Okta). No direct cloud IAM user assignments are permitted.
- Permission reviews: Quarterly entitlement review by resource owners.
- Onboarding: New hires request role group membership via the access request portal; approvals must include manager and application owner.
- Offboarding: Automated IdP deprovisioning triggers removal from groups and runs a deprovisioning playbook to revoke sessions and keys.
- Service accounts: Prefer workload identity / OIDC short-lived tokens. Long-lived keys require rotation every 90 days and documented justification.
rbac_permission_matrix:
Condensed permission matrix (service categories vs. roles). See canonical matrix in eng-infra IAM docs for full detail.

| Service Category | Owner | Infra-Engineer | Developer | Auditor | Support |
|------------------|-------|----------------|-----------|--------|---------|
| Cloud Account Admin | Full | Limited (MFA, JIT) | No | Read | Read |
| Runtime Clusters | Full | Manage | Deploy | Read | Read |
| Key Management | Full | Request-only | No | Read (audit only) | No |
| Logging & SIEM | Full | Manage | No | Read | Read |
authentication_and_idp:
- IdP: Okta as source of truth for human identities.
- MFA: Required for all interactive admin roles (hardware or TOTP + biometrics where supported).
- SSO: Enforced across Redwood Console, internal apps, and cloud consoles via central SSO.
- B2B/b2c: Customer-facing authentication separated into dedicated clusters with customer-specific controls for private deployments.
audit_logging:
- Surface: Audit logging must capture authentication events, authorization changes (RBAC grants/revocations), key material lifecycle events, API access to customer data, and administrative console actions.
- Retention: Security-critical logs retained for 1 year in hot storage; 7 years in cold/archival storage where required by contract.
- Integrity: Logs are forwarded to the centralized SIEM with tamper-evident storage (WORM / checksum).
- Monitoring: Alerts for anomalous activities (privilege escalation, sudden mass permission changes, abnormal data access patterns).
- Ownership: Eng-SRE owns SIEM ingestion pipelines; Security owns detection rules and alert triage playbooks.
data_residency_and_retention:
- Data residency: Customer data must be stored in customer-requested regions or legally required jurisdictions. Default hosted data region is us-west-2; customers can request eu-west-1 or ap-southeast-1.
- Data classification: All data must be labeled at ingress (public, internal, sensitive, regulated).
- Retention policy: Default retention for customer input & generated content is 30 days for the hosted API unless contract specifies otherwise. Audit logs and backup snapshots follow retention above.
- Data deletion: Deletion requests follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) workflow; for hosted customers, deletion within 48 hours for non-archival data after verification.
- Cross-border transfer: Transfers use approved contracts (SCCs) and encryption in transit and at rest.
- Private deployments: Customers are the data controller; Redwood provides mapping guidance and evidence for requested controls.
secure_sdlc:
- Requirements & gating: All production-facing code must pass security gates: dependency scanning (SCA), SAST, secrets scanning, container image SBOM, and SBOM policy checks.
- Code review: Two approvers required for changes touching authentication, authorization, or secrets handling.
- CI/CD controls: Pipeline credentials are stored in KMS-backed secret stores with access scoped to minimal build agents. CD deploys require signed artifacts and a deploy approval workflow for high-risk services.
- Threat modeling: Required for major features and any change that expands the attack surface (new external APIs, data egress).
- Third-party software: Approved via the OSS/commercial third-party intake process and reviewed by Security and Legal for license and security risks.
- Developer training: Annual secure-coding training required for all engineers; security champions program for teams owning critical services.
incident_response_security_procedures:
- Classification: Incidents classified by impact (SEV1–SEV4). Security incidents follow the combined oncall-and-incident-response process with additional compliance steps.
- Immediate actions: Identify scope, isolate affected services, revoke compromised credentials, enable enhanced logging, and notify on-call security.
- Communication: Use the SEV channel for technical comms and the status-page-and-comms process for customer-facing updates. Legal and Customer Success must be looped for customer-impacting incidents.
- Forensic evidence: Preserve logs and snapshots in the evidence bucket (immutable) before any remediation that could destroy volatile artifacts.
- Post-incident: Postmortem within 7 days, security review of root cause and compensating controls, and update detection/playbooks.
- Exercises: Tabletop exercises on at least a quarterly cadence; annual external penetration test and purple-team engagement.
compliance_evidence_workflows:
- Evidence catalog: Maintain an evidence catalog mapping controls to artifacts (config, logs, runbooks, policy docs).
- Requests: Compliance or external auditors submit requests via the compliance portal. Owners have 7 business days to provide evidence unless flagged urgent.
- Automation: Where possible, evidence is delivered via automated exports (IAM snapshots, log retention proofs, SIEM queries).
- Evidence types: Configuration screenshots, IAM policy exports, KMS key rotation history, access review reports, enrollment screenshots for security training, signed change approvals.
- Audit support: The Security team coordinates auditor access with time-bound read-only roles and supervised sessions for deeper reviews.
- Retention of evidence: Audit evidence retention follows business/legal requirements, default 7 years unless shorter retention contractual obligations apply.
risk_and_exceptions_process:
- Exception requests: Service owners must submit a Risk Exception Request (RER) with justification, compensating controls, and an expiration date.
- Review: Security reviews requests within 10 business days and routes high-risk exceptions to the Risk Committee (includes Security, Legal, Product, and Eng-Infra).
- Approval criteria: Acceptable compensating controls, measurable mitigations, limited blast radius, and sunset plan.
- Tracking: Approved exceptions recorded in the Exception Register with owner, risk level, mitigation, and re-evaluation date.
- Re-evaluation: Exceptions automatically re-evaluated at expiry or earlier if conditions change. Unmitigated exceptions must be remediated or escalated to executive leadership.
operational_playbooks_and_runbooks:
- RBAC change runbook: Step-by-step for requesting, approving, and applying role changes, including emergency JIT access procedures.
- Incident triage playbook: Triage checklist for suspicious auth or data access events, listed runbooks for revocation and containment.
- Evidence collection runbook: Steps to collect immutable copies of logs, database snapshots, and deployment artifacts for audits or investigations.
- Where to find them: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks and /confluence/security-and-compliance/playbooks.
metrics_and_slos:
- SLOs: Mean time to detect (MTTD) for high-confidence security events: < 15 minutes. Mean time to remediate (MTTR) for privileged-credential compromise: < 4 hours.
- Key metrics: percentage of services with periodic entitlement reviews, percentage of pipelines with SBOM+SCA, number of high-severity vulnerabilities outstanding >30 days.
- Reporting cadence: Monthly security dashboard to leadership; quarterly compliance readiness review.
references_and_tools:
- IdP: Okta; Cloud providers: AWS & GCP; SIEM: Splunk; Vulnerability management: Tenable; SAST/SCA: GitHub Advanced Security; Secrets: HashiCorp Vault; Evidence portal: Internal compliance portal.
- Related docs: eng-infra IAM best practices, security-and-compliance-playbook, incident-process, and onprem packaging docs for private deployments.
appendix:
Templates and quick commands: 
- IAM entitlement export: `aws iam get-account-authorization-details --output json > iam-snapshot.json`
- Evidence snapshot instruction: use the evidence runbook to create immutable S3 object with checksum and retention tag.
- Exception template: include risk statement, impact assessment, compensating controls, owner, and re-eval date.
